newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-LOBANOVSKY RETURNING TO DYNAMO KIEV, CLUB SOURCES SAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LOBANOVSKY RETURNING TO DYNAMO KIEV, CLUB SOURCES SAY.

text.p: Valery Lobanovsky, the former Soviet national coach who steered Dynamo Kiev to European success over 20 years ago, is on his way back to the embattled Ukrainian champions, club sources told Reuters on Thursday.
A spokesman for Dynamo, who top the league but are already out of European competition this year, would not comment but said the club planned a "very important" news conference on Friday.
Kievskiye Vedomosti newspaper said Dymano had signed a contract with Lobanovsky, who played for both Kiev and the Soviet national side, and would bring him in as head coach in the new year.

Current coach Jozhef Sabo, who was given sweeping powers to cut players' pay and bonuses in a "state of emergency" declared after last month's European defeats, will stay on till then, the paper said.
The club tried to get the 57-year-old Lobanovsky as coach in 1993, but he had already signed a contract with the Kuwaiti national side.
Under his guidance, Dynamo Kiev dominated Soviet soccer and won the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1975. They repeated the feat in 1986, the year Lobanovsky became Soviet team coach.
In all, Dynamo won the Soviet championship 13 times and the Soviet cup nine times.
But, restricted now to the Ukrainian league and with much of Ukraine's best talent preferring to play in Russia or western Europe, Dynamo have struggled.
They were banned from European soccer for three years after trying to bribe the referee in a Champions' League game against Panathinaikos last year. UEFA later lifted the suspension.
But Dynamo were knocked out of the European Cup by Rapid Vienna in the qualifying round and then went down to Xamax Neuchatel of Switzerland in the first round of the UEFA Cup.
